chunks: And by this chain, from Ali, from those who narrated it to him, that he said:

A son was born to me, so I wrote seeking permission to perform his circumcision (taher) on the seventh day. The reply came: Do not do it. He died on the seventh or eighth day. Then I wrote about his death, and the reply came: Allah will replace him with another, and name him Ahmad, and after Ahmad, Ja'far. It came to pass as he said.
ai.seo_question: What happened to Ali's son when he sought permission for circumcision from the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam's knowledge of the unseen (*'Ilm al-Ghayb*) through a specific miracle involving Ali's son, demonstrating the continuity of the Imamate line during the Minor Occultation. The prediction of 'Ahmad' followed by 'Ja'far' serves as a key identifier for the subsequent Imams, reinforcing the divine preservation of the progeny despite the brevity of the first son's life. This event underscores the theological principle that the Imam's authority extends to guiding the faithful in both religious rites and familial destiny.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 242 - It is narrated from the same chains from Ali from those who narrated it that he said: “

A son was born for me. I wrote a letter to the Master of the Age, seeking permission to perform his circumcision on the seventh day. Reply came saying not to do it. My son died on the seventh or eighth day. Then I wrote to our Master about his death. The answer came: You will sire another and another son. He named the first as Ahmad and the other Ja’far. They were born as the Imam had predicted.
